extracted.intended_audience: secondary-school math students, contest participants, coaches, and teachers
extracted.subtask_description: Compilation of problems from the All‑Soviet‑Union (final) mathematical competitions (1961–1986) intended for school pupils (forms 8–10). The page gives problem statements, meta‑information about participants, format, permitted uses, and data‑quality notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target participants and time limit
rubrics_metrics.description: "Those problems were submitted for the solving on the competition between the pupils of 8, 9, or 10 forms for 4 hours.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies intended solver age/grade (8th≈14 years) and that each contest session was 4 hours long (note: author later mentions historical two‑day finals in his experience).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of topics / curriculum bounds
rubrics_metrics.description: "So they do not contain something of the advanced topics, -- all of them can be solved by a schoolboy. They can not go out of the common school plan bounds.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Problems are intended to stay within standard school mathematics curriculum (no advanced university topics); suitability for school-level solvers is an explicit design constraint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition stages (procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The competition is held in 3 - 4 stages 1. At school ... 2. Subregional ... 3. Regional ... 4. Final part, considered in the report.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the multi-stage structure (school → subregional → regional → final) used to select finalists; useful for understanding how problems fit into the overall contest pipeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical performance expectations / assessment norm
rubrics_metrics.description: "The winners (2-5) usually give the perfect solution of all the problems with some shortages. ... It is very difficult to speak about the average level, because it depends very much on a region, but most of the participants of that time solved at least one problem. The problem is not only the difficulties in the problems themselves, but also in the shortage of time.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives an empirical benchmark for solution quality: top contestants often solve nearly all problems, average contestants typically solve at least one; time pressure is a major factor in scoring/outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permission / copyright and permitted uses
rubrics_metrics.description: "You don't need MY permission for using those problems. As concerns the copyright, the usage of all the information in the non-commercial purposes was never restricted in Russia if it is not related to the state security. ... the solutions ... belong to the authors, and the translation without their explicit permission would be their copyright violation.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author permits non‑commercial use/distribution of the problems and encourages educational reuse; warns that official solutions belong to original authors and translating/posting solutions may violate copyright without permission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data quality / conversion disclaimer
rubrics_metrics.description: "This file contains the problems ... It was semi- automatically converted from the plain text with the help of the powerful GNU emacs. Since only a few manual editing was applied (to the fractions and pseudo-graphics), there can be some stupid mistakes. Please, feel free to inform me about them.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the HTML/text was semi‑automatically converted and may contain transcription or formatting errors; users should expect and report mistakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of solutions / translations
rubrics_metrics.description: "Sorry, there exists no complete translation of the cited book. Besides, the solutions (in comparison with the problems themselves) belong to the authors, and the translation without their explicit permission would be their copyright violation.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that complete translations of official solutions are not available and that solutions are treated differently from problem statements regarding copyright and redistribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational reuse guidance / instructor discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: "You don't need MY permission for using those problems... And You only are able to decide whether Your students can solve them.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly encourages teachers/coaches to reuse problems in school projects/teaching; leaves judgment about appropriateness of items to the instructor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem-to-form mapping / formatting convention
rubrics_metrics.description: The page includes tables mapping each year's problems to forms (e.g., "form 8 001 002 003 004 005a ..."),
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an explicit assignment of numbered problems to the intended school form (8/9/10/11) and to particular competition years — useful for selecting problems by difficulty/grade and for archival reference.
